title: Shri Deepak Kumar Pamnani vs Shri Anil Kumar Lohani on 2 September, 2024
full_text: Shri Deepak Kumar Pamnani vs Shri Anil Kumar Lohani on 2 September, 2024 IN THE COURT OF Ms. HIMANSHI TYAGI JMFC(NI ACT) DIGITAL COURT-1, NORTH, ROHINI COURTS, NEW DELHI DEEPAK KUMAR PAMNANI S/o Sh. TIKAM DASS PAMNANI Add:-H.No. C-637, NEW SABZI MANDI, AZADPUR, DELHI-110033 ................Complainant Vs. ANIL KUMAR LOHANI PROPRIETOR OF JASHANMAL PARASRAM & SONS Add:- C-45, NEW SABZI MANDI, AZADPUR, DELHI-33 .......................Accused JUDGMENT CNR No. DLNT020029772021 CC NI ACT 918/2021 Date of Insititution 12.03.2021 Offence alleged Under Section 138 NI Act Plea of the accused Not pleaded guilty Final Order Acquittal Digitally signed Date of Decision 02.09.2024 by HIMANSHI HIMANSHI TYAGI Date: TYAGI 2024.09.02 17:27:32 +0530 CC NI ACT 918/2021 1 of 14 (1.) Vide this judgment I shall dispose of the complaint filed by the complainant un- der Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Act') against accused Anil Kumar Lohani. (2.) Brief facts relevant for the decision of the case are as under: The complainant has stated that the accused is running the business of of fruits as propri- etor of Jashanmal Parasram & Sons and had approached the complainant for taking loan for business purposes and after verification about the businiess goodwill and reputation of the accused in the market, the complainant had advanced a loan of Rs. 2,00,000/- to the ac- cused on 06.10.2017 through cheque no. 000080 dated 06.10.2017 drawn on Bank of Bar- oda, Inderprastha Bhawan, New Subzi Mandi, Axadpur, Delhi-33 @ 12% p.a. which was duly acknowledged and accepted by the accused and for which the accused had executed a demand promissory note and receipt both dated 06.10.2017 in favour of the complainant in acknowledge of the receiving of the aforesaid loan amount. (2.1) It is further stated in the complaint that though the loan was advanced for the period three months only, the period of the same was extended orally on payment of inter- est which had been paid upto 28.07.2020 only and thereafter neither the accused has paid the interest nor the principle amount. Ultimately on repeated demands and requests of the complainant to repay the aforesaid loan amount, the accused had issued a cheque bearing no. 440437 drawn on UCO Bank, New Sabzi Mandi, Delhi-33 of Rs. 2,00,000/- dated 04.01.2021, towards repayment of the aforesaid loan amount with assurance to pay the in- terest in cash to the complainant. Since the accused failed to pay the interest as agreed, hence the aforesaid cheque was presented by the complainant with his Bank i.e. Bank of Baroda, Inderprastha Bhawan, New Subzi Mandi, Azadpur, Delhi-33 for encashment but the same was returned by the Bank of the accused unpaid for the reason "Fund Insuffi- Digitally signed by HIMANSHI TYAGI HIMANSHI Date: TYAGI 2024.09.02 17:27:41 +0530 CC NI ACT 918/2021 2 of 14 cient" on 15.01.2021. When the complainant apprised the accused about dishonour of the aforesaid cheque, the accused requested the complainant not to take any legal action against the accused and assured the complainant to the cheque pay amount of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lac Only) with interest within ten days but failed to pay the cheque amount and the complainant got served a legal demand notice dated 12.02.2021 upon the accused through speed post and the same has been duly served upon the accused but despite receiving/knowledge of legal notice, the accused has neither made nor ten- dered any payment till date to the complainant towards the amount due against the ac- cused. Hence the complainant filed the present compliant with the prayer that accused be summoned, tried and punished according to law. EVIDENCE AND PROCEEDINGS BEFORE THE COURT: (3.) Upon appreciation of presummoning evidence, accused was summoned by the Ld Predecessor vide order dated 25.01.2022 for an offence punishable under Section 138 of the Act. Thereafter, on the 14.03.2023, notice under Section 251 Cr.P.C. for the offence u/s 138 Negotiable Instrument Act was served upon him by the Ld Predecessor to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. Further, he denied his signatures on the cheque and the receipt of legal notice. He took the defence that the firm Jashan Mal Paras Ram and Sons is of his brother Ashok Kumar Lohani and his brother has signed the cheque. He also stated that he looked after the activities of the firm till November 2019 but was no more as- sociated with the firm. Thereafter, the accused was permitted to cross examine the com- plainant and the matter was listed for evidence. (4.) The complainant led evidence by examining himself as CW-1 in post summoning evidence, wherein he adopted his pre-summoning evidence. In order to prove his case, the complainant had relied upon the Original Promissory note Ex. CW-1/1 and receipt Ex. CW-1/2 photocopy of the passbook of the complaint, original Cheque Ex.CW1/3, return memo Ex.CW1/4, Legal demand notice dated 12.02.2021 Ex.CW1/5 and receipt Digitally of speed signed by HIMANSHI HIMANSHI TYAGI TYAGI Date: 2024.09.02 17:27:44 +0530 CC NI ACT 918/2021 3 of 14 post Ex CW1/6 and Ex. CW-17 tracking report Mark- A and Mark-B. The complainant fur- ther filed additional evidence by way of affidavit i.e. audio/video conversation between the complainant and accused Ex. CW-1/9 and Ex. CW-1/10, Section 65B certificate Ex. CW-1/11. The complainant was then cross examined by the Ld. Counsel for accused. CE was closed vide order dated 24.11.2023 by the Ld Predecessor of the court. STATEMENT OF THE ACCUSED: (5.) Statement of the accused was recorded u/s 313 Cr.P.C. r/w Section 281 Cr.P.C on 19.03.2024 wherein all the incriminating circumstances appearing in evidence against the accused were put to him. The accused chose to lead evidence in his defence, and the matter was fixed for defence evidence. However, the accused thereafter chose to not lead DE and the matter was fixed for final arguments. ARGUMENTS: (6.) During arguments, it was further averred by the Ld. Counsel for the complainant that the presumption u/s 139 r/w section 118(a) of the Act arises in favour of the com- plainant, the complainant has successfully proved all the ingredients of the offence but the accused has failed to raise any probable defence in order to disprove the case of the com- plainant and has failed to rebut the presumption u/s 139 r/w section 118(a) of the Act, therefore, accused is liable to be convicted u/s 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act. (7.) Per contra, Ld. Counsel for the accused reiterated the version of the accused given in answer to the notice u/s 251 Cr.P.C as well as in his statement u/s 313 Cr.P.C. He also ar- gued that the accused is not drawer of the cheque, he is not the proprietor of the firm, he did not receive any legal notice, he had not liability towards the complainant, the complainant has failed to prove his case and therefore, accused be acquitted in this case. Digitally signed by HIMANSHI HIMANSHI TYAGI TYAGI Date: 2024.09.02 17:27:47 +0530 CC NI ACT 918/2021 4 of 14 (8.) I have carefully heard the arguments, perused the entire record as well as the evi- dence led by the complainant as well as the accused. LAW APPLICABLE: (9.) Before analysing the material on record, it is imperative to set forth the legal princi ples which governs the adjudication of cases under Section 138 NI Act. A bare reading of Section 138 NI Act reveals that in addition to the cheque being issued for the discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability; following are the ingredients which consti- tute an offence:- (i) Person must have drawn a cheque on an account maintained by him in a bank for pay- ment of a certain amount of money to another person from out of that account for the dis- charge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability; (ii)That cheque has been presented to the bank within a period of three months from the date on which it is drawn or within the period of its validity whichever is earlier; (iii)That cheque is returned by the bank unpaid, either because of the amount of money standing to the credit of the account is insufficient to honour the cheque or that it exceeds the amount arranged to be paid from that account by an agreement made with the bank; (iv) The payee or the holder in due course of the cheque makes a demand for the payment of the said amount of money by giving a notice in writing, to the drawer of the cheque, within 30 days of the receipt of information by him from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid; (v) The drawer of such cheque fails to make payment of the said amount of money to the payee or the holder in due course of the cheque within 15 days of the receipt of the said no- Digitally tice. signed by HIMANSHI HIMANSHI TYAGI TYAGI Date: 2024.09.02 17:27:50 +0530 CC NI ACT 918/2021 5 of 14 (10.) It is only when all the above mentioned ingredients are satisfied that the person who has drawn the cheque can be said to have committed an offence u/s 138 NI Act. ( Para 26, N. Harihara Krishnan vs J. Thomas , (2018) 13 SCC 663, referred to in Himanshu vs B. Shivamurthy (2019) 3 SCC 797) (11.) Section 138 is to be read with the presumption, being a rebuttable presumption, as contained in Section 139 . Section 139 provides that: "Presumption in favour of holder - It shall be presumed, unless the con- trary is proved, that the holder of a cheque received the cheque of the na- ture referred to in Section 138 for the discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability." (12.) Further, Section 118(a) deals with presumption of the cheque having been issued in discharge of a legally sustainable liability and drawn for good consideration. Section 118 of the N.I Act provides:- "Presumptions as to negotiable in- struments: Until the contrary is proved, the following presumptions shall be made: (a) of consideration - that every negotiable instrument was made or drawn for consideration, and that every such instrument, when it has been accepted, endorsed, negoti- ated or transferred was accepted, en- Digitally signed by HIMANSHI HIMANSHI TYAGI TYAGI Date: 2024.09.02 17:27:54 +0530 CC NI ACT 918/2021 6 of 14 dorsed, negotiated or transferred for consideration;" (13.) The law is also well settled that once the cheque relates to the account of the accused and he accepts and admits the signatures on the said cheque, then initial presumption as contemplated under Section 118 read with section 139 of the Negotiable Instruments Act has to be raised by the Court in favor of the complainant. ( Rangappa v. Mohan , AIR 2010 SC 1898). Reference can also be made to K. Bhaskaran vs. Sankaran Vaidhyan Balan 1999 (4) RCR (Criminal) 309, wherein it has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court as under: "As the signature in the cheque is ad- mitted to be that of the accused, the presumption envisaged in Section 118 of the Act can legally be inferred that the cheque was made or drawn for consideration on the date which the cheque bears. Section 139 of the Act enjoins on the court to presume that the holder of the cheque received it for the discharge of any debt or lia- bility." (14.) Needless to mention herein that the presumption contemplated under Section 139 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, is a rebuttable presumption. However, the onus of proving that the cheque was not in discharge of any debt or other liability is on the accused drawer of the cheque. Now, whether or not the accused has been able to rebut the said presumption is a question of fact which needs to be decided after appreciation of entire evidence led on behalf of both the parties in the light of guiding principles laid down by the Hon'ble Digitally signed by HIMANSHI HIMANSHI TYAGI TYAGI Date: 2024.09.02 17:27:58 +0530 CC NI ACT 918/2021 7 of 14 Supreme Court as mentioned herein above and depends upon the facts and circumstances of each case. BRIEF REASONS AND FINDINGS: (15.) In the present case, since the accused has not admitted his signatures on cheque in question, therefore the initial presumption in terms of Section 118 (a) and 139 of the NI Act does not arise in favour of the complainant regarding existence of legally enforceable liabililty and regarding issuance of cheque in question by the accused in favour of com- plainant in discharge of his aforesaid liability. The complainant thus, had the burden to prove these facts beyond reasonable doubts by leading cogent and reliable evidence. (16.) In order to prove the case, the complainant led his evidence by way of affidavit. The complainant examined himself as CW1/1 by way of affidavit. In his evidence the com- plainant stated that he gave a friendly loan of Rs 2, 00,000/- to the accused for which the accused even gave a promissory note Ex CW 1/1. He further deposed that accused paid the interest amount till July 2020 and later neither he paid the loan nor the interest amount. He further deposed that to discharge the liability from the loan borrowed the accused issued cheque Ex CW1/3 to the complainant with an assurance of its encashmen but the same was returned with the remarks "Funds Insufficient" vide bank return memo dated 15.01.2021. Thereafter, complainant served a legal notice Ex CW1/5 upon the accused through his counsel demanding the said amount. (17.) The defences of the accused are that he was not the proprietor of the firm "Jashan Lal Paras Ram and Sons", he did not take any loan from the complainant, did not issue the cheque to the complainant and did not receive any notice of demand. Since, the accused has chosen not to examine himself as a witness or lead defence evidence, the defence of the accused has to be seen in the light of cross-examination of the complainant. Digitally signed by HIMANSHI HIMANSHI TYAGI TYAGI Date: 2024.09.02 17:28:01 +0530 CC NI ACT 918/2021 8 of 14 (18.) Coming to the first ingredient of the offence, which is that the drawer of the cheque should have issued the cheque for the discharge, in whole or in part of a legally enforce- able debt or other liability, it is stated by the complainant that the complainant had ex- tended a loan of Rs. 2,00,000/- to the accused who had issued the cheque in question to the complainant for the discharge of his legally recoverable liability, however, upon presenta- tion, the cheque in question had got dishonoured. (19.) Upon analyzing the statements of the accused recorded u/s 251 Cr.P.C and Section 313 Cr.P.C. what comes out is that the accused has not admitted the cheque to be issued by him or his signatures on the cheque. As per the version of the complainant, the accused is the proprietor of the firm Jashan Mal Paras Ram and Sons. However, the same has been denied by the accused. He even took the defence in his statement u/s 271 CrPC as well in his examination u/s 313 CrPC that the proprietor of the firm is his brother and he had only maintained the accounts of the firm till 2019. In this scenario, to prove the liability, the burden was upon the complainant to show that accused was the proprietor of the firm Jashan Lal Paras Ram and Sons. (20.) The careful perusal of the record shows that the complainant has not filed any doc ument to show that the accused was the proprietor of the firm. In this regard, it is pertinent to note that drawer of the cheque Ex CW1/3 is "Jashan Mal Paras Ram and Sons", a firm. Moroever, the promissory note Ex CW1/1 as well the receipt of the loan Ex CW1/2 are in the name of the above mentioned firm. Perusal of the printout of the bank statement of the complainant which also shows that the cheque through which loan was allegedly ad- vanced by the complainant, was credited to "Jashan Mal Paras Ram and Sons". So none of the documents brought on record show that he is the proprietor of the firm "Jashan Mal Paras Ram and Sons" or reflect the accused to be the beneficiary of the loan advanced. (21.) In his cross examination, the complainant deposed that as per his belief, the accused was the proprietor. He even deposed that the cheques given by the accused Digitally for the payment signed by HIMANSHI HIMANSHI TYAGI Date: TYAGI 2024.09.02 17:28:04 +0530 CC NI ACT 918/2021 9 of 14 of the interest amount were duly honoured so he did not doubt that the account did not be- long to the accused. To elucidate the stand of the complainant on these aspects, the rele- vant questions and the answers put to him in his cross examination are quoted as under: "It is mentioned in para-3 of your PSE affidavit that you have verified about the good- will and reputation of the acused, did you verified who is the proprietor of Jashanmal Parasram and sons? Ans. Mr. Anil Kumar is the proprietor. (Vol. All the business dealing and transactions used to take place with him). Que. Did you take any security at the time of advancing of loan? Ans. No. (Vol. I took receipt and a promissory note from Mr. Anil Lohani. I was told that he was the proprietor). Que. Who told you that Mr. Anil Lohani is the proprietor? Ans. He himself represented himself as the proprietor, further, all the cheques given by him for payment of interest used to get cleared before the bank. Therefore, there was no scope of suspicion in my mind that he is not the proprietor." (22.) The above portion of the cross examination clearly shows that the complainant has only relied upon his belief and he has neither brought any document nor has examined any witness to show that the accused was the proprietor of the firm. The complaint claimed that the other cheques issued by the accused were duly encashed so he never doubted that accused is not the proprietor. But the complainant has not placed the so called cheques for payment of interest to buttress his claim of his this belief. No presumption can be drawn in this case that the cheque in question pertained to the accused's bank account merely be- cause of the encashment of other cheques issued by the accused. It is well known rule of Digitally signed by HIMANSHI HIMANSHI TYAGI TYAGI Date: 2024.09.02 17:28:08 +0530 CC NI ACT 918/2021 10 of 14 law that a belief, however strong, substitute of evidence. Moreover, the complainant has not proved by way of any other oral or documentary proof that loan of Rs 2,00,000/- was indeed advanced to the accused himself. No independent witness to the advancing of the loan or handing over of the cheque in question has examined by the complainant. (23.) Further, the signatures on the cheque had not been admitted by the accused so the burden was upon the complainant to prove that the accused was the drawer of the cheque. However, no bank official was examined by the complainant to show that accused was the signatory of the cheque in question. (24.) Further, the audio video recording relied upon by the complainant to prove the ad- mission of the debt by the accused is not sufficient to discharge the burden of the com- plainant. The perusal of the transcript of the CD shows that the audio does not mention anything about the cheque number or the other details of the case. Also, the CD of audio- video recording furnished by way of additional evidence have admittedly been recorded post filing of the present case and is stated to contain the admission of the accused regard- ing the liability. In this context, it is essential to note that the contents of the CD were never played before the court. Furthermore, such admission of the liability cannot be relied upon by the court as there is nothing to show that the accused made such admission voluntary and without fear, force or coercion. (25.) On account of the above mentioned reasons and observations, this court is of the view that the complianant has failed to prove that the accused is the proprietor of the firm Jashanmal Parasram and Sons , that the accused had signed the cheque and that there is a legally recoverable debt against the accused. The complainant failed to prove the first in- gredient of the offence. (26.) The second condition qua the presentation of the cheque within three months is sat isfied upon the perusal of the cheque in question Ex CW1/3 which is dated 04.01.2021 Digitally signed by HIMANSHI HIMANSHI TYAGI TYAGI Date: 2024.09.02 17:28:12 +0530 CC NI ACT 918/2021 11 of 14 while the return memo Ex.CW1/2 is dated 15.01.2021. It is abundantly clear that the cheque was presented within the prescribed period of limitation of three months. The de- fence did not adduce any evidence whatsoever to contradict the same. (27.) The third ingredient of the offence is that the cheque is returned by the bank unpaid, either because of the amount of money standing to the credit of that account is insufficient to honour the cheque or that it exceeds the amount arranged to be paid from that account by an agreement made with that bank. 27.1 The cheque in question upon presentation in the bank was dishonoured on 15.01.2021. A perusal of Ex.CW1/4 shows that the cheque in question, on being presented in the bank was returned dishonoured due to "Funds insufficient". Bank return memo or slip is prima facie proof of dishonor. Section 146 of the NI Act, in this regard comes into play which raises a presumption that the court shall presume the fact of dishonor of the cheque in case of cheque is returned vide a return memo issued by the bank having thereon the official mark denoting that the cheque has been dishonored. Again, as the defence has failed to rebut the said presumption, hence the said condition is also satisfied. Thus, in the opinion of the court, the second ingredient of the offence is also met in the present case. 27.2 As far as the fourth ingredient of the offence is concerned, the postal receipts as well as the track report of the receipt of the legal notice are present on record which show that legal notice dated 12.02.2021 was dispatched on 12.02.2021 and thus, this con- dition also stands satisfied. (28.) The last condition is that accused fails to make the payment within fifteen days from the date of the receipt of the legal demand notice. The accused has denied the receipt of le- gal notice. Digitally signed by HIMANSHI TYAGI HIMANSHI Date: TYAGI 2024.09.02 17:28:15 +0530 CC NI ACT 918/2021 12 of 14 28.1 In this context, it is incumbent to note that the the mandatory requirement of issue of notice in terms of clause (b) of proviso to Section 138 of N.I.Act stands complied with if the payee has dispatched the notice by registered post with correct address of the drawer of the cheque and the principle incorporated in Section 27 of the General Clauses Act would be attracted. The complainant has sent the legal notice on the complianant had addressed his legal notice to the address mentioned on the promissory note Ex CW1/1. The accused has not disputed the address mentioned on the legal notice or on the promissory note, though he has denied the service of the notice. Further, in light of the judgment C.C. Alavi Haji Vs Palapetty Muhammed & Anr 2007 (6) SCC 555 passed by Hon'ble Apex court, the defence of not receiving the notice is not maintainable if the accused does not pay amount of the cheque to the complainant within 15 days of receiving the summons from the court. The accused did not do so in the present case and has failed to adduce any evidence to rebut the presumption of due service. Therefore, the accused is deemed to be served under section 138 N.I. Act. (29.) In the case at hand, the complainant did not have the presumption of law in his favour under section 118 and 139 of NI Act since accused denied his signatures on the cheque in question, hence, the burden was on the complainant himself to prove that the cheque in question was drawn in his favour to discharge the liability of the cheque amount. However, complainant has miserably failed to do so. On the other hand, The defence taken by accused has remained intact throughout the proceedings whenever his statement in this regard was recorded such as at the time of framing of notice, during cross examination of complainant and at the time of his statement recorded under section 313 Cr.P.C, 1973. (30.) In view of the foregoing discussion, this Court is of the considered view that the complainant has been unable to prove the first ingredient of the offence regarding accused being the drawer of the cheque in question and the cheque being issued for a legally en- forceable liability. The complainant could not successfully prove his case against the ac- Digitally signed by HIMANSHI HIMANSHI TYAGI TYAGI Date: 2024.09.02 17:28:18 +0530 CC NI ACT 918/2021 13 of 14 cused for the offence under Sec. 138 NI Act beyond reasonable doubts. Resultantly, the accused is acquitted for the said offence. As per section 437-A Cr.P.C accused is admitted to bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.10,000/- with one surety of like amount. (31.) Ordered accordingly.
